learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the invisible stretch! Understand how solid materials deform under pressure, what makes steel more elastic than rubber, and how engineers design safe bridges.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Elasticity is a material's ability to completely regain its original shape after a deforming force is removed (like a spring). Plasticity is when a material is permanently deformed and doesn't snap back (like chewing gum).

Stress is the internal restoring force applied per unit area ($F/A$). Strain is the fractional change in dimension caused by that stress (like Change in Length / Original Length). Stress is the cause; Strain is the effect.
For small deformations, Stress is directly proportional to Strain. The ratio of Stress to Strain is a constant called the Modulus of Elasticity.

1. Young's Modulus ($Y$) measures resistance to changes in length. 2. Shear Modulus ($G$) measures resistance to shape distortion. 3. Bulk Modulus ($B$) measures resistance to changes in volume under pressure.

A graph showing how a wire behaves when stretched. It has a Proportional Limit (obeys Hooke's law), an Elastic Limit (snaps back), a Yield Point (starts permanently deforming), and finally a Breaking Point.

fun_activity.title: 🧠 Steel vs. Rubber
fun_activity.instructions: If you ask someone which is more elastic, steel or rubber, they will say rubber. But in physics, Steel is MUCH more elastic! Why? Because Elasticity means the ability to RESIST deformation and return to normal. It takes vastly more stress to stretch steel than rubber.

exam_tips: 📌 Drawing and labeling the Stress-Strain curve perfectly (Proportional limit, Yield point, Breaking stress) is a high-probability exam question.
📌 Know the formula for the Elastic Potential Energy stored in a stretched wire: $U = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Stress} \times \text{Strain} \times \text{Volume}$.
📌 Liquids and gases only have Bulk Modulus. Only solids have all three (Young's, Shear, and Bulk) because fluids cannot sustain shear stress.
quick_recap: ⭐ Stress has the exact same dimensional formula as Pressure ($[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$).
⭐ Strain is a dimensionless quantity because it is a ratio of two identical units.
⭐ Elastomers (like the rubber in a balloon) can be stretched massively without breaking, but they do not strictly obey Hooke's Law.
